gotchas.title: Client and procedure say 'qualifying widower'
gotchas.trap: File 2025 as Qualifying Surviving Spouse (procedure wording) or Single.
gotchas.correct_treatment: In the year of death the survivor files MFJ (sec. 6013(a)(2)); QSS needs a dependent child and only applies to the 2 following years. Harold has no dependent -> 2026 onward Single. Sign as surviving spouse; no Form 1310. Procedure is imprecise - follow the law.

gotchas.procedure_section: Estate Implications - step-up in basis (community property)
gotchas.title: Schwab 1099-B shows original cost; noncovered lots show no basis
gotchas.trap: Use the 1099-B/original cost (gain $347,120), zero basis on noncovered lots, or step up only Eleanor's half (gain $179,254).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Washington community property: BOTH halves get a date-of-death basis (sec. 1014(b)(6)); holding period long-term. Use the Schwab DOD valuation (weekend DOD - mean of adjacent trading days). Box D with code B adjustment for the covered MSFT lot; box E with DOD basis for noncovered lots. Gain $11,387.
gotchas.impact: Sch D overstated $335,733 (~$50,360+ tax and a WA excise filing)

gotchas.procedure_section: Estate Implications - sale of a home received from an estate; Schedule D code H
gotchas.title: 1099-S $685,000 on the marital home
gotchas.trap: Compute gain from the 1998 cost ($338,227) and apply a $250,000 single exclusion -> $88,227 taxable; or omit the sale because it is excluded.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Full community-property step-up to the $615,000 appraisal -> gain $18,227; excluded under sec. 121 ($500,000 - MFJ in year of death; sec. 121(b)(4) would also give $500k within 2 years of death). A 1099-S was issued, so report on Form 8949 box F with code H and the exclusion as a negative adjustment.
gotchas.impact: Up to ~$99k of gain wrongly taxed

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule A - medical; decedent's expenses; funeral
gotchas.title: Final medical bills and funeral costs
gotchas.trap: Skip itemizing (standard + 65 add-ons looks 'normal' for retirees), deduct the funeral, or miss the Medicare premiums on the SSA-1099s.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Medical $48,710 (hospital, residential hospice room & board, licensed home aide under a plan of care, Medicare Part B from both SSA-1099s, Medigap/Part D) less 7.5% floor -> itemized $52,845 > standard $34,700. Funeral is never a 1040 deduction.

gotchas.title: Eleanor's August benefit returned
gotchas.trap: Enter box 3 gross benefits ($16,605) for Eleanor.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Use box 5 net benefits ($14,760) - the repayment is netted in the same year (no sec. 1341 claim needed). Total line 6a $45,960.

gotchas.title: Vanguard statement shows a $418,903 'transfer out' of Eleanor's IRA
gotchas.trap: Report the spousal transfer as an IRA distribution on line 4a/4b.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Direct trustee-to-trustee transfer by the surviving spouse who elected to treat the IRA as his own - not a distribution, no 1099-R, nothing on line 4. Only Harold's own $10,000 withdrawal is taxable.

gotchas.title: Deceased spouse and the new $6,000 senior deduction
gotchas.trap: Claim only one senior deduction (Harold) because Eleanor died, or skip it because they itemize.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Both spouses were 65+ and the deduction is allowed whether or not itemizing; MAGI $95,881 < $150,000 -> 2 x $6,000 = $12,000.

gotchas.procedure_section: Estate Implications / SALT - WA capital gains excise; Form 706 portability
gotchas.title: Items outside the 1040
gotchas.trap: Ignore; or file a WA capital gains excise return based on unadjusted gains.
gotchas.correct_treatment: With stepped-up basis, 2025 LTCG $11,387 is far below the ~$278,000 WA standard deduction (home sale exempt) - no WA filing. Flag to signer: a portability-only Form 706 (DSUE election) for Eleanor's estate - due 05/09/2026 (+6 months with Form 4768) or late under Rev. Proc. 2022-32 until 08/09/2030. Engagement for the 706 is a separate project.
